qa.question: If this card's effect reduces the number of cards in my deck to 0, do I lose the game?
qa.answer: No, you don't lose the game when your deck is empty. You will lose the game if your deck has 0 cards in it at your next draw phase, however.

qa.question: Can this Digimon attack if I have less than 2 memory?
qa.answer: Yes, it can. Even if your memory counter moves to 1 on your opponent's side due to this Digimon's [When Attacking] effect, your turn doesn't end until the attack does.

qa.question: Can this Digimon attack if I have less than 2 memory?
qa.answer: Yes, it can. Even if your memory counter moves to 1 on your opponent's side due to this Digimon's [When Attacking] effect, your turn doesn't end until the attack does.

qa.question: Can I use this card's effect to give this Digimon <Retaliation>?
I use this card to give a Digimon <Retaliation>. If that Digimon digivolves into a different Digimon, what happens to <Retaliation>?
qa.answer: Digimon retain effects when digivolving or de-digivolving, so <Retaliation> remains.

qa.question: I use this card's <Digi-Burst> to trash a purple level 3 Digimon card in the Digimon with <Digi-Burst>'s digivolution cards. Can I immediately use the <Digi-Burst> effect to play that Digimon without paying its memory cost?

I use this card's effect to delete one of my Digimon with a [When Deleted] effect. Can I activate the [When Deleted] effect before this card's "delete 1 of your opponent's level 4 or lower Digimon" effect?
qa.answer: No. You must fully activate this card's effect, then activate the [When Deleted] effect.

qa.question: I use this card to delete one of my own Digimon, and an opponent's Digimon. If they both have [When Deleted] effects, which effect resolves first?
qa.answer: They activate at the same time, which means the turn player resolves their effect first.

qa.question: Can I use this card's effect if I only have either a level 3 or level 4 purple Digimon card in my trash?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. If you only have a level 3 or level 4 purple Digimon card in your trash, you can play it.

qa.question: What cards can be played using this card's [Main] effect?
qa.answer: 1 purple level 3 Digimon card and 1 purple level 4 Digimon card.

comprehensive-0223.title: <Blocker>
comprehensive-0223.text:
16-5. <Blocker>
16-5-1. <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
16-5-2. <Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-5-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.

comprehensive-0226.title: <Draw>
comprehensive-0226.text:
16-8. <Draw>
16-8-1. <Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.
16-8-2. <Draw> effects execute processing.
16-8-3. A draw from <Draw> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0231.title: <Retaliation>
comprehensive-0231.text:
16-13. <Retaliation>
16-13-1. <Retaliation> is a keyword effect where a battled opponent's Digimon is deleted when a Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle.
16-13-2. <Retaliation> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when just the Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-13-3. The processing from <Retaliation> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0232.title: <Digi-Burst>
comprehensive-0232.text:
16-14. <Digi-Burst>
16-14-1. <Digi-Burst> is a keyword effect where another effect specified by this effect will activate by trashing the specified number of digivolution cards from the Digimon with this effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digi-Burst 1>.
16-14-2. The processing from <Digi-Burst> is optional. For details, refer to 15-6 "Processing Conditions")
